title: The tensor-formula pullback of modules is left adjoint to pushforward
statement: Let $g:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], viewed as a morphism of locally ringed spaces [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism] with ring map $g^\sharp:\mathcal O_Y\to g_*\mathcal O_X$. For a sheaf of $\mathcal O_Y$-modules $\mathcal G$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], its inverse image sheaf $g^{-1}\mathcal G$ [def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image] has the $g^{-1}\mathcal O_Y$-module structure induced from the action on $\mathcal G$. Set $P_g\mathcal G=\mathcal O_X\otimes_{g^{-1}\mathcal O_Y}g^{-1}\mathcal G$ using the sheaf tensor product and change of rings [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. The assignment $P_g$ extends to a functor on module sheaves, acting on a morphism $u:\mathcal G\to\mathcal G'$ by $\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal O_X}\otimes g^{-1}u$. For a sheaf of $\mathcal O_X$-modules $\mathcal F$, define $g_*\mathcal F$ on opens $V\subseteq Y$ by $(g_*\mathcal F)(V)=\mathcal F(g^{-1}V)$, with its $\mathcal O_Y(V)$-action restricted along $g^\sharp_V$. Then the natural map $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_X}(P_g\mathcal G,\mathcal F)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_Y}(\mathcal G,g_*\mathcal F)$ obtained by tensor/restriction of scalars and inverse-image/direct-image adjunction is a bijection, natural in both modules. Consequently $P_g$ is left adjoint to $g_*$.

proof.text: Write $\rho:g^{-1}\mathcal O_Y\to\mathcal O_X$ for the adjoint of $g^\sharp$ [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism, def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image], and let $\mathcal F_0=\operatorname{Res}_{\rho}\mathcal F$, the sheaf $\mathcal F$ viewed as a $g^{-1}\mathcal O_Y$-module. The inverse image $g^{-1}\mathcal G$ has its $g^{-1}\mathcal O_Y$-action by [lem-pc-module-inverse-image-adjunction]. By the formula defining $P_g$ and the change-of-rings adjunction [lem-pc-module-change-of-rings-adjunction] (with $\mathcal A=g^{-1}\mathcal O_Y$, $\mathcal B=\mathcal O_X$, $\mathcal M=g^{-1}\mathcal G$, $\mathcal N=\mathcal F$), there is a natural bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_X}(P_g\mathcal G,\mathcal F)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{g^{-1}\mathcal O_Y}(g^{-1}\mathcal G,\mathcal F_0)$. On a map $u$ it sends a local section $m$ to $u(1\otimes m)$.

source.place: Tag 0096, lemma-adjoint-pullback-pushforward-modules, proof: first equality; Tag 008A, lemma-adjointness-tensor-restrict

proof.text: Apply the natural inverse-image/direct-image module adjunction [lem-pc-module-inverse-image-adjunction] with $f=g$, $\mathcal A=\mathcal O_Y$, $\mathcal M=\mathcal G$, and $\mathcal N=\mathcal F_0$. This gives $\operatorname{Hom}_{g^{-1}\mathcal O_Y}(g^{-1}\mathcal G,\mathcal F_0)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_Y}(\mathcal G,g_*\mathcal F_0)$, where the $\mathcal O_Y$-action on $g_*\mathcal F_0$ is through $\eta_{\mathcal O_Y}:\mathcal O_Y\to g_*g^{-1}\mathcal O_Y$.

source.place: Tag 0096, lemma-adjoint-pullback-pushforward-modules, proof: second equality; Tag 008Y, lemma-adjoint-push-pull-modules

proof.text: For every open $V\subseteq Y$, $g_*\mathcal F_0(V)=\mathcal F(g^{-1}V)$ as abelian groups [def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image]. Its $\mathcal O_Y(V)$-action from step 2 sends $a\in\mathcal O_Y(V)$ and $s\in\mathcal F(g^{-1}V)$ to $\rho_{g^{-1}V}(\eta_{\mathcal O_Y,V}(a))s$. Since $\rho$ is adjoint to $g^\sharp$, $\rho_{g^{-1}V}\circ\eta_{\mathcal O_Y,V}=g^\sharp_V$ [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism, def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image]; thus the action is exactly $g^\sharp_V(a)s$, the action defining $g_*\mathcal F$ in the statement. The identity of section groups is therefore an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_Y$-modules $g_*\mathcal F_0=g_*\mathcal F$. Compose this identification with the two bijections from steps 1 and 2. Each is natural in both module variables by the cited statements, and the identification is natural in $\mathcal F$ by its sectionwise formula. Their composite is the asserted natural Hom bijection, hence the adjunction $P_g\dashv g_*$.
